text.title: Nasdaq slips as Nvidia CEO exit hits chips; yields climb, bitcoin falls
text.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.9%, while the Dow edged up 0.1%. Tech dropped 2.0% as Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia pulled down chip stocks, and defensive sectors rose. The Nasdaq still posted its best week since August, according to CNBC.

drivers.t: Nvidia has had its longest weekly losing streak since 2012, with about $1.7 trillion in market value lost since early October, and Colette Kress is now interim CEO. AMD and other chip stocks also slid as investors rethought the AI trade without Huang.

The technology sector fell 2.0% as the Nvidia turmoil spilled into the wider semiconductor group. Consumer staples (+1.4%), communication (+1.1%) and financials (+0.8%) rose, which helped keep the Dow positive.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5 bp to 5.15% and the 2-year rose 2 bp to 4.88%. WSJ said rate fears resurfaced, even though CNBC noted the latest inflation data came in slightly lighter than expected.
MarketWatch said Huang's exit is weighing on Chinese tech stocks. He was seen as an influential voice for selling chips to Chinese companies, and investors are preparing for more restrictions.
Bitcoin fell 4.2% to about $68,342, dropping below $69,000. MarketWatch said investors may sell crypto holdings to make room for the Anthropic IPO.

watch: Anthropic's IPO is expected next week, and it will try to take SpaceX's title as the biggest public listing ever.
